question: Where were the 2008 Commonwealth Youth Games primarily hosted?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Pune **__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **2008 Commonwealth Youth Games** were primarily hosted in **Pune, Maharashtra**, India. It was the third edition of the Commonwealth Youth Games.
 
• The event took place from **12th to 18th October 2008**, and it showcased the participation of young athletes from various Commonwealth nations.
 
• The Games saw the participation of around **1,300 athletes** and officials from 71 Commonwealth countries competing in various disciplines.
 
• **Shree Shiv Chhatrapati Sports Complex**, located in Balewadi, Pune, was the main venue for the Games. The facility was renovated and modernized to international standards for this purpose.
 
• The event featured **9 sports disciplines**, including athletics, swimming, badminton, boxing, table tennis, shooting, tennis, wrestling, and weightlifting, providing a platform for young athletes to showcase their talent.
 
• The Games were significant for promoting **youth sports** and fostering international camaraderie among the Commonwealth nations.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Background and Significance of the Commonwealth Youth Games:**

 
 
• The **Commonwealth Youth Games** aim to provide young athletes (aged 14–18) a platform to compete at an international level and prepare for larger multi-sport events like the Commonwealth Games or the Olympics.
 
• The first edition of the Commonwealth Youth Games was held in **Edinburgh, Scotland, in 2000**, followed by the second edition in **Bendigo, Australia, in 2004**.
 
• The Games also play a crucial role in promoting the values of the Commonwealth, including **friendship, equality, and inclusivity**.
 
 
 
• **Shree Shiv Chhatrapati Sports Complex:**
 
 
• This sports complex, situated in **Balewadi, Pune**, served as the main venue for the 2008 Commonwealth Youth Games.
 
• The complex underwent a major renovation to meet international standards, including facilities for multiple sports, advanced infrastructure, and seating arrangements for spectators.
 
• It continues to host various national and international sporting events, making it a significant sports hub in India.
 
 
 
• **Participants and Sports:**
 
 
• The 2008 edition saw participation from **71 Commonwealth countries**, with over **1,300 young athletes** competing.
 
• The Games featured **9 disciplines**: athletics, badminton, boxing, swimming, shooting, table tennis, tennis, wrestling, and weightlifting.
 
• The event was a stepping stone for many athletes who later went on to achieve success in senior-level competitions.
 
 
 
• **India’s Role:**
 
 
• Hosting the 2008 Commonwealth Youth Games was a matter of pride for India, showcasing its ability to organize international multi-sport events.
 
• The successful hosting of the event also served as a precursor to India hosting the **2010 Commonwealth Games** in New Delhi.
 
• India performed exceptionally well in the Games, clinching **33 gold medals** and securing the **top position** in the medal tally.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Legacy of the 2008 Commonwealth Youth Games:**

 
 
• The Games left a lasting legacy in terms of **sports infrastructure** in Pune, with facilities that continue to benefit athletes and sports enthusiasts.
 
• The event boosted **India’s reputation** as a capable host for international sporting events.
 
• It also inspired increased participation and interest in sports among Indian youth, contributing to the country’s overall sports development.
 
 
 
• **Comparison with Other Editions:**
 
 
• The 2008 Games were notable for their **efficient organization** and the enthusiastic participation of athletes and spectators alike.
 
• While the earlier editions (2000 in Edinburgh and 2004 in Bendigo) set the foundation, the Pune Games raised the bar in terms of **scale and impact**.
